subtopics.title: Factors, Not Terms — the Cancelling Law

questions.question: In an algebraic fraction you may cancel:
options: Any x that appears above and below
A factor that the whole numerator and the whole denominator share
Any term that appears above and below
The largest number in each line

questions.question: Fully factorised, x² − 9 over x² + 7x + 12 becomes:
Simplified, x² − 9 over x² + 7x + 12 equals:
Substituting x = 1 into the original expression and into a proposed answer is used to:
options: Convert the fraction to a decimal
Test whether a cancellation was legal — the two values must match

subtopics.title: Multiplying, Dividing, and Denominators Hiding Cubes

questions.question: When dividing one algebraic fraction by another, the first move is to:
options: Invert the second fraction and multiply

questions.question: x² − 4 over x + 3, divided by x + 2 over x² − 9, simplifies to:
x³ − 8 over x² − 4 simplifies to:
Why does the answer x² + 2x + 4 over x + 2 stop there?
options: Because cubes may never be simplified
Because the numerator is larger than the denominator
Because the 2x and the x are not like terms
Because x² + 2x + 4 does not factorise — no two whole numbers multiply to 4 and add to 2

subtopics.title: Adding and Subtracting — the Lowest Common Denominator

questions.question: The lowest common denominator of 3 over (x − 3) and 2 over (x² − 9) is:
3 over (x − 3) minus 2 over (x² − 9) simplifies to:
(2x + 1) over (x − 4) minus (x − 3) over (x − 4) equals:
A learner writes 2x + 1 − x − 3 for that numerator instead of x + 4. The error is:
options: Adding instead of subtracting the denominators
Using the wrong lowest common denominator
Cancelling a term instead of a factor
Failing to bracket the numerator being subtracted, so the minus was not distributed to the −3

questions.question: Restrictions on the variable must be read from:
options: The numerator of the original expression
The original denominators, before any cancelling

questions.question: For x² − 9 over x² + 7x + 12, the full restrictions are:
options: x ≠ −4 only, since x + 3 cancelled away

questions.question: A denominator equal to zero makes the fraction:
Which statement belongs in the error museum?
options: 3 over x plus 2 over (x + 1) equals 5 over (2x + 1)
Leave the denominator in factor form

subtopics.title: You Can Only Cancel a Whole Crate

questions.question: In the stockroom picture, a 'loose bottle' on top stands for:
options: A factor that can be cancelled
A plus or minus sign — a term that is not part of a packed block

questions.question: Factorising is described as:
options: Repacking a messy pile into neat crates multiplied together
Sharing the pile among the customers
Cutting the pile into smaller slices

questions.question: Substituting x = 1 gave −2 over 5 for both the original and the answer. This means:
options: The answer must still be factorised further
The simplification preserved the expression's value — the check balances

subtopics.title: Cut the Slices the Same Size Before You Add

questions.question: In the bread analogy, the denominator represents:
To rewrite 3 over (x − 3) over the denominator (x − 3)(x + 3), you:
options: Multiply numerator and denominator by (x + 3), giving 3x + 9 on top

questions.question: The returned-packet picture (one loaf and three rand owing) teaches that:
options: Denominators may be added when they match
Fractions can be added without a common denominator
Subtracting a numerator with two terms reverses BOTH terms — bracket it first

questions.question: Multiplying a fraction's top and bottom by the same bracket:
options: Changes only how it is cut, not its value

subtopics.title: The Numbers the Fraction Will Not Allow

questions.question: Sharing R240 among zero learners has no answer. In algebra this corresponds to:
options: A denominator equal to zero — the expression is undefined

questions.question: After (x + 3) cancels away, why is x = −3 still banned?
options: It was refused at the door by the original expression, and tidying up cannot un-ban it
Because negative values of x are never allowed
It is not banned once it cancels

questions.question: The four moves of a complete answer, in order, are:
options: Factorise; cancel whole factors; cut to a common denominator and bracket any parcel subtracted; state restrictions from the original denominators
State restrictions; add numerators; add denominators; cancel
